subject: Staggered commit failsafe and repricing protocol for Exhibit A (caps/floors)
messages:
From: Sara Patel <procurement@brighthealth.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightHealth Legal <legal@brighthealth.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Exhibit A questions: caps, floors, and emergency repricing

David —

Thanks again for the draft Exhibit A attached. A couple of items our procurement & ops teams flagged that we need clarified before we can move to legal redlines:

- If we see a sudden spike (e.g., a one-week 5x increase in token consumption due to a campaign or misconfiguration), how does the cap/floor mechanism behave? Is there an automatic repricing or throttling?
- We need a clear failsafe that prevents an unexpected spike from immediately triggering a long-term floor or accelerating us into a higher tier without human review.
- For partial reductions (we might scale commits down by 30% mid-quarter), how does the true-up/proration work operationally?

Can you send the operational playbook or proposed wording for a "failsafe rollback" and an example rollback matrix? We want thresholds, notification windows, and any credits applied during the grace period.

Attaching the version of Exhibit A we received. Would prefer to resolve with short, specific language rather than a freeform negotiation.

Sara
Sara Patel
Procurement Lead, BrightHealth
procurement@brighthealth.com
Attachment: BrightHealth_ExhibitA_v1.docx (attachment: pricing exhibit draft)

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <procurement@brighthealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exhibit A questions: caps, floors, and emergency repricing

Sara — thanks for the clear list. High-level response and next steps below. I'll loop in Legal for precise contract language.

High-level behavior we propose:
- Staggered commit with failsafe: sudden week-over-week usage spikes will not automatically rebase your committed tier. We implement a 7-day median filter for short-term anomalies and require sustained usage over a trailing 30-day window before moving you to a higher committed band.
- Emergency repricing trigger: we can include a temporary surcharge path (30-day emergency surcharge) that applies only when usage exceeds the cap by >200% week-over-week AND is sustained for 14 consecutive days; human ops review required before any longer-term repricing.
- Rollback matrix and grace credits: if we apply a temporary surcharge and later determine spike was anomalous, we will credit the surcharge pro rata and revert tier changes retroactively to the start of the anomaly window.
- Proration & true-up: partial commit reductions mid-quarter will be prorated on a daily basis with a true-up at the following invoice cycle. We can add minimum notice windows for reductions to avoid churn (suggested 14 days).

Next steps: Marissa, can Legal draft redline language that captures the 7-day median, 30-day sustained window, the emergency surcharge guardrail, and credit/rollback mechanics? Jonas, can you attach the internal ops playbook (runsheet) that shows how we detect anomalies and who gets the alert?

Sara — happy to jump on a 30-minute call with your ops and legal teams tomorrow afternoon if that helps.

Best,
David Kim
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
david_kim@redwood.com
Attachment: RDW_Operational_Playbook_Anomaly_Detection.pdf (internal playbook stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Patel <procurement@brighthealth.com>, BrightHealth Legal <legal@brighthealth.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 10:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exhibit A questions: caps, floors, and emergency repricing

All — I reviewed David's outline and prepared a concise set of redline edits to insert into Exhibit A. I attached a marked-up file (Redline_ExhibitA_MCo_20261102.docx). Key legal points summarized below for your review before I send to BrightHealth as proposed contract language: 

1) Definitions (new):
- "Usage Anomaly": an increase in billed token consumption that exceeds 200% of baseline weekly usage, subject to confirmation by our telemetry (7-day median).
- "Failsafe Window": a 14-day period following the detection of a Usage Anomaly during which automatic tier reclassification is suspended and human review is required.

2) Failsafe & Repricing Mechanics (replace existing paragraph):
- Short-term anomalies will be evaluated under the 7-day median filter. No automatic upgrade to a higher committed tier will occur unless usage exceeds the stated cap for 30 consecutive days.
- A temporary emergency surcharge (not to exceed 25% of per-token fees) may be applied for up to 30 days where usage exceeds the cap by >200% and where sustained infrastructure pressure would otherwise materially affect Redwood service. Prior to applying any surcharge, Redwood will provide written notice to Customer and trigger the Failsafe Window.
- If the Usage Anomaly is later determined to be non-recurring or caused by Customer misconfiguration that is remediated within the Failsafe Window, Redwood will refund or credit any emergency surcharge applied on a pro rata basis and will not reclassify Customer to a higher committed tier retroactively.

3) Partial reductions & true-up (clarify):
- Customer may request a reduction to committed volume with 14 days' notice. Reductions will be prorated daily and reconciled at the next invoice. If Customer requests reductions that are inconsistent with prior commitments in a way that would cause material forecast disruption, Redwood may require a good-faith discussion and a phased reduction over no less than 30 calendar days.

4) Notice & Dispute (new):
- Any surcharge or tier reclassification is subject to dispute within 30 days of notice. Disputes will follow the escalation path in Section 6 (Ops -> Sales -> Legal) and, during dispute resolution, surcharges may be temporarily suspended pending investigation.

Marissa's ask: David/Jonas — confirm the operational detection thresholds above match what Ops will enforce (7-day median + 30-day sustained trigger + 14-day Failsafe Window). Also confirm we can limit emergency surcharge to 25% (ops input on capacity/costs appreciated).

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Commercial
marissa_cole@redwood.com
Attachment: Redline_ExhibitA_MCo_20261102.docx (marked redline of Exhibit A)

From: Sara Patel <procurement@brighthealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightHealth Legal <legal@brighthealth.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exhibit A questions: caps, floors, and emergency repricing

Marissa / David —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the specific redlines. BrightHealth Legal reviewed and we can accept the majority of the proposed language with two counterpoints: 

1) We need a minimum 30-day notice (rather than 14) for Customer-initiated reductions that affect committed volume. Our procurement cadence requires a longer window for downstream teams.
2) For emergency surcharges, we request that any surcharge be capped at 15% rather than 25% and that it be subject to automatic referral to an independent technical review if the surcharge exceeds 10% to confirm it is not caused by Redwood's telemetry/configuration error.

If you can accept those two changes, we will have our GC sign the revised Exhibit A and route the DocuSign envelope. Otherwise please outline what you can do on the notice and cap adjustments and we'll iterate.

We are available to sign provided the two adjustments above.

Sara Patel
Procurement Lead, BrightHealth
procurement@brighthealth.com
DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/en/documents/BH-0472-exhibitA-sign
